description: Reviewed upper bounds for direct production access to the legacy disease_records projection. Counts may decrease but must never increase without an explicit architecture review.

admin_explorer.description: Administrative, read-only table inspection retained during the migration window. It must not become a public analytical source.

compatibility_projection.description: Controlled series-first projection that temporarily reads legacy rows only for explicitly labelled fallback or coverage-gap filling.

deprecated_tool.description: Already deprecated legacy utility retained only until its replacement and recovery documentation are complete.

developer_diagnostic.description: Local developer diagnostic that is not part of a deployed data or API path.

historical_import.description: Historical import or rebuild path that still targets the flat compatibility table and must be replaced by the source-series ingestion service.

migration.description: Audited migration, backfill, canonicalization, or restore code allowed to inspect or mutate legacy rows while the table remains recoverable.

quality_audit.description: Legacy-specific parity or data-quality audit retained for migration verification, not as the authoritative quality layer.

runtime_read.description: Deployed API, report, crawler checkpoint, export, or agent read that must be migrated to the shared series-first query service.

runtime_write.description: Temporary live compatibility projection writer or legacy checkpoint reader; writes must remain transactionally paired with source-series facts until disabled.

schema_contract.description: ORM, relationship, schema-generation, or cleanup contract retained until the final read-only archive and table removal phase.
